items.summary: CRO handoff: retain three evidence-backed opportunities as deferred backlog only. (1) microsoft/markitdown (MIT): prototype offline document-to-Markdown extraction for content QA on one existing repository; evidence: 22 keyword hits, 8/8 bounded checks passed, 194 files; risks: dependency provenance, parser accuracy, maintenance, and no production adoption; metric: extraction accuracy and editor time saved; time-to-learn: 1–2 days; smallest reversible prototype: fixture-only conversion script. (2) shadcn-ui/ui (MIT): prototype one accessible CTA/card component for a queue-ready site; evidence: 3/3 bounded checks passed, 3,198 files; risks: framework compatibility, dependency/supply-chain review, maintenance, and visual regression; metric: deterministic accessibility/build checks and CTA interaction rate using existing telemetry; time-to-learn: 1–2 days; smallest prototype: isolated preview component. (3) mermaid-js/mermaid (MIT): prototype one source-backed diagram in an editorial explainer; evidence: supported use case, 2,799 files, but no safe native checks; risks: client bundle/performance, rendering reliability, maintenance, and content accuracy; metric: page engagement and web-vitals using existing telemetry; time-to-learn: 1–2 days; smallest prototype: static offline-rendered SVG fixture. Do not install dependencies, deploy, add telemetry, spend, or requeue until existing measurement, failure-repair, ownership, security, release, rollback, attribution, and validation gates clear. Current evidence supports no revenue, ROI, or conversion-lift claim.
